_about: Parameter experiments of formulation 4. Each experiment changes ONE factor at a time (one variant = one change); every other input stays as in the baseline. A variant is applied with --set overrides when the solver reads the data: no data or parameter file is copied. The baseline itself is NOT solved again: the analysis takes it from baseline_MILP/results (run milp_300s) and baseline_RL/results (run rl_f4). Folder names: <folder>_MILP and <folder>_RL inside 2026-11-22_formulation_4/. Priority 1 runs first (user, 22 Nov 2026: E5 and E6 first, then E1, E2, E8). Experiment numbers are those of the experiment table (comprehensive report, Section 4.14 extensions).

instances._about: Same instance set as the baselines: the 56 Solomon files at n = 10, 20, ..., 100 = 560 instances.

solver._about: Settings of the experiment runs = the baseline runs, so a variant differs from the baseline only in its input. RL: rl_f4_zero_shot = the baseline model applied to the variant's inputs; rl_f4_retrained = a new model trained on the variant (same recipe as the baseline training).

experiments.name: Value of charging time at theta = 1
experiments.question: How sensitive is the van share (per segment) to the most influential assumed value?
experiments._about: Personal: c^{C,1} (value of a minute of FCS charging at the top income), the most influential value in formulation 3. Commercial: the downtime rate at theta = 1 (D = C = V, and Q with it), the commercial counterpart; it is scaled as a whole so that D = C = V still holds. +-25 %.

experiments.name: Money sensitivity at theta = 0, mu^0
experiments.question: How sensitive are Z and the van share to the coefficient with the largest elasticity on Z?
experiments._about: mu^0 of each segment separately, +-25 % (mu^1 = 0.5 stays, so mu stays non-increasing).

experiments.name: Van tariff p^M
experiments.question: Who gets vans (per segment and income), and at what cost to the operator and to equity?
experiments._about: p^M = 15 equals the FCS tariff p^F (no van premium); 35 doubles the premium.

experiments.name: Van fleet and seats (one at a time)
experiments.question: Where does another van or seat pay off, and where is capacity idle?
experiments._about: Number of vans |M| (config n_vans) and EVs per van Q (config van_max_evs) for every Solomon file.

experiments.name: Van battery upper bound B
experiments.question: Is recharging worth modelling? If Z barely moves, drop it.
experiments._about: B = 200 kWh for every van. If the mean change of Z on paired instances stays below decision_threshold_pct, a larger battery (or recharging) changes little and van recharging need not be modelled.

experiments.name: Station capacity (charging points and power)
experiments.question: How do changes in station capacity -- the number of charging points per station and the power per point -- affect the optimal solution (cost, queues, van use)?
experiments._about: Rubric factor 'station capacities'. Two levers, one change per variant: the number of guns per fixed charging station (config.guns_per_station, baseline 2) and the charging power per gun in kW (config.station_power_kW, baseline 22). Applied in memory with --set (no data copy). Fewer or weaker guns make the fixed stations a tighter bottleneck (longer queues, slower charging), which should push more EVs onto vans and raise Z; more or stronger guns do the reverse. Power enters tau^F = 60 E / P^F, so it shortens every FCS session without adding parallel capacity.

experiments.name: Charging demand (energy per EV)
experiments.question: How does a change in charging demand -- the energy each EV needs -- affect the optimal solution? (The demand LEVEL, i.e. the number of EVs, is the n = 10..file-size sweep itself and is reported separately.)
experiments._about: Rubric factor 'charging demand'. The energy need E_i of every EV is multiplied by config.energy_scale (baseline 1.0). This scales both charging times (tau^F = 60 E / P^F at a station, tau^M by a van) and the energy drawn, so more energy per EV lengthens every session, tightens both the stations and the vans, and should raise cost and queues; less does the reverse. +-25 %. The RL generator applies the same scale when a variant model is retrained (rl_f4_generator.energy_scale).
